solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: See 23 down
Sea creature's audible cry?

indicators.note: audible says the word for a cry is to be heard, not read, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a wail is a long mournful cry

explanation.surface: A question about what noise some marine animal makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audible' says a word meaning 'cry' (WAIL) is heard, and it sounds like the creature's name. The possessive 's on the definition is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest marine mammals are sea-dwelling animals.

clue.text: Celebrity from Asian country, a gem

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
of can mean from, as in 'a man of Kent'
India is a country in South Asia

explanation.surface: A famous person hailing from somewhere in Asia turns out to be precious.
explanation.definitionFit: The Star of India is a famous large star sapphire held in a New York museum.

clue.text: Quip from individual on ship

parts.note: a single individual is one
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Someone on an ocean voyage makes a witty remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link, placing one piece next to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A short witty remark delivered in a single sentence is a quip.

clue.text: Latest 8, faulty, unaccountably

indicators.note: faulty suggests something broken and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 8 down, a dynamo

explanation.surface: The newest power unit is defective for no apparent reason.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' stands for the answer to 8 down; with LATEST it gives fifteen letters for 'faulty' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase used when something happens oddly and without explanation, so it is said in an inexplicable way.

clue.text: Condescend to hold second draw

indicators.note: to hold means the first word takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: to deign is to condescend

explanation.surface: Someone stoops to holding a second drawing in a game or lottery.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw is to sketch or plan, a verb sense of design.

clue.text: Chitty put together by English leader of team

parts.note: spacecraft dock when they are joined together

indicators.note: leader of picks out the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A note of payment compiled by an English team captain.
explanation.walkthrough: A chitty is a British word for a short note or voucher, such as a receipt or a pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A docket is a document or label recording goods or payment, much like a chit.

clue.text: Agree to judge at close quarters

parts.note: to see can mean to judge or consider, as in 'as I see it'
eye to eye describes being face to face, very close up

explanation.surface: Someone consents to give a verdict while standing very near.
explanation.definitionFit: To share the same view as someone is to concur with them, a common idiom.

clue.text: Dynamo in garret one fixed

indicators.note: fixed suggests something rearranged or doctored, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An electric machine kept in an attic that someone has repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; 'fixed' rearranges GARRET ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a machine producing electricity, a kind of electrical generating device.

clue.text: Flask in restaurant containing a drop of red

indicators.note: containing says the restaurant word holds the next pieces

parts.note: a cafe is a small restaurant

indicators.note: a drop of something is a small first bit, so only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A wine vessel served in an eatery with a splash of red wine in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is an open-topped glass bottle for serving wine or water, a type of flask.

clue.text: Enter car sprayed yellow

indicators.note: sprayed suggests letters scattered about, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Get into a vehicle that has been painted yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yellow' looks like the paint colour but means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: A recreant is a craven, cowardly person, and yellow is slang for cowardly.

clue.text: Check Volvo's rear red light

parts.note: to vet is to check thoroughly

indicators.note: rear points to the back end of the word, its last letter

explanation.surface: Inspecting the tail light on a Volvo car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red light' looks like part of the car but is a figurative stop signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is a refusal or ban, figuratively a stop signal.

clue.text: Landlords in the north needing minders

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for north
keepers are people who mind or look after something

explanation.surface: Property owners in the north of the country need bodyguards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Landlords of pubs or inns are the keepers of those premises.

clue.text: Clown in magazine, in magazine with no hat on

parts.note: Punch was a British humour magazine
taken as written

indicators.note: with no hat on means the word loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: Hello! is a British celebrity magazine

explanation.surface: A clown appears in a magazine without a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch was a British satirical weekly; Hello! is a British celebrity magazine, which loses its H. The first 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Punchinello is the hook-nosed buffoon of Italian puppet comedy, a classic clown figure.

clue.text: Mother in lead close to home — hallelujah!

indicators.note: in places the mother word inside the lead word

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
to mother a child is to raise it

indicators.note: close to here means the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A mother in charge on her way home cries out with joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother' looks like a noun but works as a verb meaning to bring up.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of thanksgiving to God.

clue.text: Make a mistake supporting cycle tour

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting puts the mistake word below the cycle word

parts.note: a cycle of events is a round
to trip is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone slips while backing a cycling tour.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey out and back again is a sort of tour or excursion.

clue.text: Be mindful of college turning

indicators.note: turning says the college name is read backwards

parts.note: Eton is a famous English school, Eton College

explanation.surface: A warning to pay attention to a college changing its ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to take heed of it.

clue.text: Half-naked look could make one daydream

indicators.note: half takes only the first part of the word for naked

parts.note: starkers is British slang for naked
to gaze is to look steadily

explanation.surface: Glimpsing someone partly undressed could set a person fantasising.
explanation.walkthrough: STARKERS is informal British for stark naked; its first half is STAR. 'could make one' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To stargaze is to be lost in idle fantasies, like a dreamer looking up at the sky.

clue.text: Play diamonds to secure kitty

parts.note: play for amusement is fun
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: A card player leads diamonds to win the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' is a link; 'kitty' is a pool of money, not a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a pool of money held in common, a reserve.

clue.text: Avant-garde? Not here — in that place

explanation.surface: A question about experimental art followed by directions elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconventional ideas are described as way off the mainstream; the phrase also means in a distant location.

clue.text: Small number on team upset inventor

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the pieces are turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A little-known number on a side causes upset to a famous inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the whole of NO SIDE, giving the American inventor of the phonograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American who patented the light bulb and the phonograph.

clue.text: Humorist given a pair of kings

parts.note: Edward is the name of several English kings
Lear is Shakespeare's legendary king of Britain

explanation.surface: A comedian is dealt two kings in a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian writer was famous for nonsense verse and limericks.

clue.text: Almost evening? Almost

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: night is the evening time

explanation.surface: A question whether it is nearly evening, answered with a near-yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh means near or nearly, an old-fashioned word for close.

clue.text: Why goose stood awkwardly in nursery tale

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests clumsy disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child's story asks why a goose was standing in an ungainly way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; 'awkwardly' rearranges WHY GOOSE STOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of an eighteenth-century children's story, later used for a smugly virtuous person.

clue.text: Man located here is, I hear, upset about son

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go round the next piece
upset signals the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tells of a mother upset about her son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I hear' looks like a sound-alike signal but is just anagram fodder. Man is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man lies in the stretch of water between Great Britain and Ireland.

clue.text: Model in Naples, Italy

indicators.note: in says the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A fashion model is working in southern Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' is a verb: to model for an artist is to pose.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit for a painter is to pose for a portrait.

clue.text: Flourishing in a period of rapid economic growth with pounds invested

indicators.note: invested means the pounds are put inside, like money placed in a venture

parts.note: a boom is a time of rapid economic growth
L is the abbreviation for pounds, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: An economy thrives in boom times once money is put into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants in bloom are blossoming, figuratively thriving.

clue.text: Completely accurate with old golf club around Troon, initially

indicators.note: around means the club word goes round the next letter

parts.note: a spoon was an old wooden golf club with a lofted face

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A golfer hits a perfect shot with antique clubs at Troon.
explanation.walkthrough: Troon is a Scottish golf course that has hosted the Open Championship.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning exactly right, hitting the mark precisely.

clue.text: See 7 down
